messages:
clare: quick sync 1: staging showed a huge uptick in tiny spans after model-X deploy. queue depth + p99 spiked. Two ops paths: aggressive edge sampling vs coalescing noisy spans + emit metering. pros/cons?

jin: sampling is fast but irreversible for postmortems. coalescing preserves analytics but moves work to gateway.

nashwin: coalesce + metering seems ideal if we can still bill accurately. need a reconciliation path when tenant resolution is late.

marta: ops: gateway CPU and memory are concerns. coalescing changes envelope sizes and shard loads. we need soft caps per-tenant.

clare: draft hybrid: cheap pre-sample (40%) at gateway, compute light fingerprint, keep tiny per-tenant reservoir (ttl 5m) of raw traces. after enrichment, run rules to resurrect important traces (errors/latency/anomaly).

jin: for billing: emit small metering events (tenant, window, token_sum, count, provisional) separate from trace aggregates. run a reconciliation job to finalize provisional events.

nashwin: dedupe/backfill semantics: use canonical trace_id + ingest_fingerprint. reservoir should be tenant-fair (soft quotas). reconciliation window ~1h is acceptable.

marta: I'll prototype a wasm normalizer for cheap fingerprinting (goal <1us/span). avoid heavy regex.

clare: action items: ashwin->reservoir/backfill proto; jin->metering + recon job; marta->wasm POC; clare->schedule follow-up. ingest-bot: alert at 3789999123 correlates with spike.

clare: keep rollout conservative and monitor provisional vs final billing in Console. :thumbsup:
